# `render/shaders/modules/compute/gpu_tile.js`

> **Source:** `engine/render/shaders/modules/compute/gpu_tile.js`

GpuTile - WebGPU workgroup shared-memory tile (WebGPU equivalent of NVIDIA cuda-tile) Inspired by: https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-tile CONCEPT: Every thread in a workgroup cooperatively loads one element of a global buffer into fast workgroup-shared memory ("the tile"), then ALL threads process the cached tile before advancing to the next tile.  This amortises global-memory latency across the whole group — the same idea that makes tiled matrix-multiply orders of magnitude faster than naive O(N²) reads. CUDA term         WebGPU/WGSL equivalent ─────────────     ───────────────────── __shared__        var<workgroup> template<T,N>     JS class with type / tileSize parameters (build-time) __syncthreads()   workgroupBarrier() threadIdx.x       @builtin(local_invocation_id) USAGE (JavaScript side, shader build-time): import { GpuTile } from ".../modules/compute/gpu_tile.js"; const bodyTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'bodyTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); const shader = ` // --- module scope --- ${bodyTile.declareWGSL()} @compute @workgroup_size(64) fn cs(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3u, @builtin(local_invocation_id)  lid: vec3u) { let i   = gid.x; let myPos = bodies[i].pos.xyz; var acc = vec3f(0.); ${bodyTile.tiledLoopWGSL({ bufExpr:   'bodies',        // storage buffer binding name elemExpr:  'b.pos',         // expression to extract from element countExpr: 'u.count', lidExpr:   'lid.x', bodyWGSL: ` for (var k = 0u; k < _bodyTile_len; k++) { let b = ${bodyTile.getWGSL('k')}; let d = b.xyz - myPos; acc += d / (dot(d,d) + 0.01); }` })} } `; ADVANCED — multiple simultaneous tiles: Give each a unique `name` so their var<workgroup> identifiers don't collide. const posTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'posTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); const velTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'velTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); // In shader: ${posTile.declareWGSL()} ${velTile.declareWGSL()}

### `class GpuTile`

GpuTile - WebGPU workgroup shared-memory tile (WebGPU equivalent of NVIDIA cuda-tile) Inspired by: https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-tile CONCEPT: Every thread in a workgroup cooperatively loads one element of a global buffer into fast workgroup-shared memory ("the tile"), then ALL threads process the cached tile before advancing to the next tile.  This amortises global-memory latency across the whole group — the same idea that makes tiled matrix-multiply orders of magnitude faster than naive O(N²) reads. CUDA term         WebGPU/WGSL equivalent ─────────────     ───────────────────── __shared__        var<workgroup> template<T,N>     JS class with type / tileSize parameters (build-time) __syncthreads()   workgroupBarrier() threadIdx.x       @builtin(local_invocation_id) USAGE (JavaScript side, shader build-time): import { GpuTile } from ".../modules/compute/gpu_tile.js"; const bodyTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'bodyTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); const shader = ` // --- module scope --- ${bodyTile.declareWGSL()} @compute @workgroup_size(64) fn cs(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3u, @builtin(local_invocation_id)  lid: vec3u) { let i   = gid.x; let myPos = bodies[i].pos.xyz; var acc = vec3f(0.); ${bodyTile.tiledLoopWGSL({ bufExpr:   'bodies',        // storage buffer binding name elemExpr:  'b.pos',         // expression to extract from element countExpr: 'u.count', lidExpr:   'lid.x', bodyWGSL: ` for (var k = 0u; k < _bodyTile_len; k++) { let b = ${bodyTile.getWGSL('k')}; let d = b.xyz - myPos; acc += d / (dot(d,d) + 0.01); }` })} } `; ADVANCED — multiple simultaneous tiles: Give each a unique `name` so their var<workgroup> identifiers don't collide. const posTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'posTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); const velTile = new GpuTile({ name: 'velTile', type: 'vec4f', tileSize: 64 }); // In shader: ${posTile.declareWGSL()} ${velTile.declareWGSL()}

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `declareWGSL` | `declareWGSL()` | Module-scope workgroup shared-memory declaration. Paste this once, outside any function, at the top of your compute shader. |
| `loadWGSL` | `loadWGSL(bufExpr, baseExpr, lidExpr, countExpr, elemExpr = null, elemVar = 'b')` | Cooperative single-element load + barrier. Each invocation loads one element; call this inside a tile loop before processing.  Inserts `workgroupBarrier()` so the tile is fully populated before any thread reads it. |
| `getWGSL` | `getWGSL(k)` | Expression to read element `k` from the tile. |
| `barrierWGSL` | `barrierWGSL()` | Trailing workgroupBarrier() to protect the tile from being overwritten before all threads finish reading.  Call after the inner processing loop. |
| `tiledLoopWGSL` | `tiledLoopWGSL({ bufExpr, countExpr, lidExpr, elemExpr = null, elemVar = 'b', bodyWGSL })` | Generate a complete outer tiled-loop that: 1. Iterates over the buffer in tiles of `tileSize` elements 2. Cooperatively loads each tile into workgroup memory 3. Executes your inner `bodyWGSL` with access to the tile 4. Emits the trailing barrier before moving to the next tile Inside `bodyWGSL` you have access to: _<name>_base  - tile start index in the global buffer _<name>_len   - number of valid elements in this tile (≤ tileSize) Use `this.getWGSL('k')` to read element k from the tile. |
| `toString` | `toString()` | Return a summary string useful for shader comments / debugging. |

### `TILED_NBODY_EXAMPLE_WGSL()`

Ready-to-paste WGSL string demonstrating the 64-thread tiled N-body pattern. This is the same code used in the playground N-Body demo, expressed via GpuTile.

## Constants

- `VEC4_TILE_64` — vec4f tile, 64 threads — matches the N-Body pattern exactly
- `VEC4_TILE_128` — vec4f tile, 128 threads — good for higher-throughput passes
- `F32_TILE_64` — f32 tile, 64 threads — useful for scalar reduction passes
- `VEC2_TILE_64` — vec2f tile, 64 threads — 2-D positions / UVs

## Notes & Examples

### Shared GPU device

Engine subsystems should reuse the cached `GpuDevice` wrapper returned by `getGpuDevice()`. The wrapper owns the native `GPUDevice`, its queue, granted features, limits, and device-loss callbacks. Resources created by one native device cannot be used by another, so pass the shared wrapper or native device into each subsystem that needs GPU access.

**Example: Acquire the shared engine device**
```js
import { getGpuDevice } from '/engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js';

const gpu = await getGpuDevice({
  label: 'MyEngineApp',
  adapterOptions: { powerPreference: 'high-performance' },
  requiredFeatures: []
});

const device = gpu.getDevice();
const queue = gpu.getQueue();
```

Request a feature only when the application cannot run without it. `GpuDevice.create()` automatically requests the engine's supported optional feature set, while `gpu.getCapabilities().features` reports the features actually granted to the device.

**Feature and limit checks**
```js
const { features, limits } = gpu.getCapabilities();

if (features.has('timestamp-query')) {
  console.info('GPU timestamp queries are available');
}

const requestedBytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
if (requestedBytes > limits.maxBufferSize) {
  throw new RangeError('Requested buffer exceeds maxBufferSize');
}
```

**Device loss**
```js
gpu.onDeviceLost((info) => {
  console.error('WebGPU device lost:', info.reason, info.message);
  // Stop work and re-bootstrap the application so every GPU resource is rebuilt.
});
```

**Gotchas:**
- **First acquisition defines requirements:** `getGpuDevice()` caches the wrapper. Supply mandatory features and limits on the first call.
- **Native access:** use `gpu.getDevice()` and `gpu.getQueue()` when a subsystem needs WebGPU primitives.
- **Recovery:** this module reports device loss but does not expose an in-place `recreate()` API. Re-bootstrap all device-owned resources together.
- **Limits:** check the granted `gpu.getCapabilities().limits` before large allocations.

(Source: `engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js`)
